name: navidrome-mood
author: 312.dev
description: Judges every track with an LLM and writes ten mood tags into the audio files: five 0-100 axes (energy, valence, intensity, acousticness, density), how fast it feels, whether it is sung, two to four mood words, the times of day it suits, and the vibe regions it falls in. Navidrome smart playlists and any Subsonic client can then filter on feeling instead of on genre.

http.reason: Send track metadata to the LLM provider you configure, and nothing else. No requiredHosts is declared so any public endpoint you point it at works, including a local OpenAI-compatible server, while loopback and private addresses stay blocked.

library.reason: Find your music, and write the mood tags directly into the audio files. Nothing else in the file is modified: audio bytes are never decoded, re-encoded, or moved, and the write is refused if the STREAMINFO checksum block would change.

kvstore.reason: Remember spend so far, how much work is queued, and where the last check for new music got to. That is a few hundred bytes whatever the library's size: what has been labelled is recorded in the files themselves. The 8MB is headroom for an older version's per-track entries, which this one deletes as it finds them; a library of 9,000 left about 1.6MB of them, and a store over its allowance refuses every write including the spend counter.

scheduler.reason: Run the periodic check for newly added music, on the interval you set. Navidrome exposes no scan-completed hook, so polling is the only way to label new tracks without you starting a run by hand.

taskqueue.reason: Run labelling as resumable background work. Each plugin invocation is capped at 30 seconds by Navidrome, so a whole-library pass has to be many small tasks rather than one long one.

provider.title: Who does the labelling
provider.description: Anthropic is the default and needs only an API key. OpenAI-compatible covers OpenAI, OpenRouter, Groq, Together, DeepSeek, and local servers like Ollama or LM Studio.

apiKey.title: API key
apiKey.description: Stored by Navidrome and sent only to the provider above.

maxSpendUsd.title: Most this run may cost (USD)
maxSpendUsd.description: A hard stop, not an estimate. Actual spend is measured from each reply and labelling halts when this is reached. A library of about 9,000 tracks costs roughly $15 with the default model.

lifetimeCapUsd.title: Most this plugin may EVER cost (USD)
lifetimeCapUsd.description: A ceiling across every run, which never resets. The per-run limit above starts fresh when you change the model or the limit, so this is what stops repeated runs adding up to a number you did not intend.

run.title: Label my library
run.description: Start with 'sample': it labels 20 tracks from across your library for a few cents so you can see whether you like the results. 'everything' labels every track that is not already carrying a full set of mood tags. Work is queued and survives restarts, and setting this back to 'off' does not cancel work already queued.

dryRun.title: Preview only, do not change my files
dryRun.description: Labels are generated and saved to the log, but nothing is written to your music files. Note this still costs the same to run, because the labels are still produced: it protects your files, not your bill. Turning it on caps a run at 20 tracks whatever Label my library says, because a preview over a whole library buys the same answer as a sample for the price of the whole library.

skipTagged.title: Leave existing mood tags alone
skipTagged.description: Skips any track that already has a mood, including ones written by Picard, beets or by hand. Turn it off to send those through labelling, which also replaces whatever wrote them. Tracks already carrying the full set of ten tags are skipped either way, because redoing them would cost money and change nothing.

autoSync.title: Label new music automatically
autoSync.description: Checks for newly added tracks and labels them without you doing anything. A check costs nothing when there is nothing new, so this is safe to leave on.

autoSyncCron.title: How often to check
autoSyncCron.description: Cron expression. The default checks every 15 minutes.

model.title: Model
model.description: Leave blank for a sensible default. Required for OpenAI-compatible providers.

batchSize.title: Tracks per request
batchSize.description: Lower this if labelling fails with a truncation message. Bounded by Navidrome's 30 second limit per plugin call, not by the provider.

batchMode.title: Use the cheaper batch API
batchMode.description: About half price, but results arrive over minutes to hours rather than immediately.

selfTest.title: Self test
selfTest.description: Diagnostic. 'read' opens one file and reports what it found. 'write' also writes a marker tag, reads it back, removes it and checks the removal. Useful if tagging is not working.
